title: Carbonation Depth (Square Root of Time)

K.description: Carbonation coefficient (depends on w/cm, CO₂, RH)

applicability: K typically 1–5 mm/√year for normal quality concrete. K > 5 for poor concrete (high w/cm, poor curing). K < 1 for high-quality, low permeability concrete with SCMs.

title: Fick's Second Law — Chloride Diffusion

C(x,t).description: Chloride concentration at depth x and time t

applicability: Assumes constant C_s and D_a (simplification). D_a decreases over time for SCM concrete. Typical D_a: 1–50 × 10⁻¹² m²/s depending on w/cm and SCMs.

title: Time to Corrosion Initiation
applicability: Rearrangement of Fick's law solved for time. C_th typically 0.05–0.10% by mass of concrete (≈ 0.2–0.4% by mass of cement).
source: Service life modeling — fib Model Code, Life-365

title: Equivalent Alkali Content
applicability: Low-alkali cement: Na₂O_eq ≤ 0.60%. Used for ASR prevention.

title: Freeze-Thaw Durability Factor

P_n.description: Relative dynamic modulus of elasticity at N cycles

N.description: Number of cycles at which P reaches 60% or 300 cycles (whichever first)

applicability: DF ≥ 60% (some specs require ≥ 80%) after 300 cycles is considered satisfactory. Relative dynamic modulus measured by ASTM C215 (resonant frequency).

title: Sorptivity

i.description: Cumulative water absorption per unit area

applicability: Measures capillary suction rate. Lower sorptivity = lower permeability. Typical initial sorptivity: 0.1–1.0 mm/√min for good concrete.

title: RCPT Chloride Permeability Rating
equation: Q = ∫₀ᵗ I dt (total charge in coulombs over 6 hours)

title: Time-Dependent Diffusion Coefficient

D_ref.description: Diffusion coefficient at reference time t_ref

m.description: Aging exponent (0.2–0.6 for OPC; 0.4–0.8 for SCM concrete)

applicability: SCM concretes show greater reduction in D over time (higher m). Critical for realistic service life prediction.
source: fib Model Code for Service Life Design (2006), Life-365

title: Corrosion Rate — Faraday's Law
applicability: Converts corrosion current density to physical steel loss. i_corr < 0.1 μA/cm² = passive; 0.1–0.5 = low; 0.5–1.0 = moderate; > 1.0 = high corrosion.

title: ASR Expansion Limit (ASTM C1260)
equation: Expansion classification: < 0.10% at 14 days = innocuous; 0.10–0.20% = inconclusive; > 0.20% = potentially deleterious
applicability: Accelerated test — mortar bars in 1N NaOH at 80°C. Fast but can be overly aggressive (false positives). Supplement with C1293 concrete prism test (1 year, < 0.04%).
